text:
meera: Customer tenant-aurora just escalated — p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~210ms to ~1.2s after the deploy at 10:12 UTC. They sent a few request IDs: r-0a1b2c r-0a1b2d. Screenshot of their dashboard: https://console.redwood/tenants/aurora/panels/abc :eyes:

sam: ONCALL - can you grab traces + raw histograms? which panel are they looking at?

meera: They linked the per-route latency panel (team:api -> model:small-fp16). Our internal raw histogram (logs) for the same window shows p99 ~420ms. The observability panel shows 1.18s.

jess: Assigned. I can repro a small uptick on a few routes in prod - seeing a handful of requests with long server-side queuing. Not consistent across pods though.

alex: Posting the two queries used by the panels:
```
# dashboard panel A (rollup-derived quantile)
derive_quantile(0.99, latency_ms, window=5m, rollup=true)

# raw histogram (panel B)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

sam: That exact mismatch smells like rollup vs raw histogram semantics. Rollups store shard-level summaries that can bias tail when sampling windows overlap. Did the deploy change our batching flag or sampling rate?

meera: Deploy toggled `enable_continuous_batching=true` and bumped batch size limit from 32 -> 64. Customer says traffic steady though.

jon: If batching increased, heavier internal queuing could create occasional long tail spikes that show up amplified in route-level rollups. Also, our rollup service uses 1m aggregation buckets and applies quantile on aggregated summaries — that can double-count long tails for low-cardinality routes.

sam: Agreed. Two parallel tracks: (1) mitigation for customer & (2) observability reconciliation. For mitigations: revert batching flag for their tenant (we can pin tenant config) or throttle the route to force smaller batches. Which we prefer?

meera: Customer wants quick fix — please pin to old config if easy. They said latency impacts user-facing chat timeouts.

alex: I can carve a per-tenant override in env for Aurora and roll it in 2m. Also add a temporary circuit that falls back to smaller batch size when queue depth > 8.

sam: Do it. Also open a short incident in incident tracker. @oncall-bot create-incident "tenant-aurora latency tail" severity=P2

oncall-bot: Incident #INC-2026-112 created, severity P2, assigned to oncall. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-112

jess: Observability note: the dashboard we have for customers uses rollup_quantile to make it cheaper. For internal ADHOC we query raw histograms — both are valid but produce different numbers under heavy batching tails. I'll file a docs note.

meera: For the reconciliation, customers are confused why our console shows 1.2s but their logs show 420ms. We should add a tooltip explaining "rollup vs raw histogram" and surface sampling config.

jon: Also double-check rollout of a kernel-level change we shipped in the same deploy — could have changed NVMe IO latencies for cold model chunks. I have a probe running across a few hosts.

alex: Done — pinned tenant config to old batching and deployed. Monitoring now shows p95 ~180ms and p99 dropping to ~430ms for the past 3m in raw traces. Dashboard rollup still shows ~1.1s until next rollup window completes.

meera: I told the customer we pinned their config and we expect visible improvement in traces; dashboard may lag up to 10m due to rollup TTL. They acknowledged and asked for postmortem.

sam: Next steps:
- alex: keep per-tenant pin for 24h and monitor tail heatmap
- jess: doc update + add tooltip to customer panel explaining metric derivation and expected rollup lag
- jon: continue infra probes for kernel/IO anomalies and report by EOD
- meera: collect customer logs for 1h post-fix, escalate if not improved

jess: One more: we should add a low-cost "tail audit" that periodically computes raw-histogram quantiles for high-traffic tenants and flags >2x divergence vs rollup. I'll prototype.

meera: Customer pleased with temp fix, will verify over next hour. Closing loop afterwards. :white_check_mark:
